description: A cairn that got up. Moss on every weathered face, a flat head low in the shoulders, one fist that opens ground.
lore: Every field anybody ever worked was cleared first, and every cleared field kept its heap: rounded brown stones at the edge of the ground, added to a little each season, walked around for a lifetime, never once taken from. Enough of that, in enough fields, and one of the heaps has a face in it. Add to it and welcome — travellers still set a stone on its shoulder in passing, the way you would on any cairn, and it takes no notice. Take from it, even one stone, and you meet the fist. A heap only ever grew. Being taken from is the thing that was never done to it.

People chance the fist anyway, because in the fall of a broken one there is sometimes raw [[lore/the_gold_agreement|gold]], and a pocket of gold buys a great deal of nerve. [[characters/7a779de1|Wendell]] refuses to call that a fair trade. On the old east road there is a Mosscairn carrying, third down from the crown, a flat grey stone he set there himself — one trip a year, forty years of trips, back when the road was safe and he still walked it. His waymark is out there yet, riding the shoulder of a thing that walks a road he no longer dares. Bring him word of where it stands now and he will sit you down at his fire until you have heard the whole road, mile by mile, the way it was.
gm_notes: Ready hook: find which Mosscairn carries Wendell's flat grey waymark; the reward is not an item, it is Wendell's east road told at length (and his company debt). The gold-in-the-rubble clause is the deliberate wiring of the_gold_agreement into a fight people actually pick.
